title: Console triage matrix & May grooming notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick, operational triage for the console & rollout backlog to form a pragmatic sprint cutlist for mid-May. This doc captures the matrix we used in the grooming session, per-ticket rationale, proposed acceptance criteria, and wireframe notes for the higher-impact items.

TL;DR:
- Triage session 2025-05-07 with PM + Eng + UX. Goal: pick scoped set of items for the May 2-week sprint (May 19 start).
- Outcome: 7 primary tickets to include (3 high-impact/low-effort, 2 medium-impact/medium-effort, 2 stretch items).
- Wireframes: two small UI changes (route-level latency table + quick-rollout toolbar) that need engineering signoff on data availability.

What we used: prioritization matrix (Impact vs Effort):
- Impact = downstream customer pain + revenue/SLAs + frequency (how often teams hit it).
- Effort = eng time + infra coordination + UX polish.
- Rule of thumb: pick all high-impact/low-effort (H-L), some medium-impact/low-effort (M-L), and 1 high-impact/high-effort (as a spike).

Grooming notes (ticket level):
1) RW-7203: Route-level latency breakdown table (H-L)
- Summary: Add per-route token-latency histogram and 95th/99th percentiles in the console route page.
- Why: CS reported repeated escalations; customers cannot pinpoint slow routes. Reduces debugging time.
- Proposed scope: read-only table + single chart + hover tooltip. No annotation/alerting this sprint.
- Wireframe notes: small foldable panel under route details, 3-column table (route, p95, p99) + sparkline.
- Acceptance criteria: data surfaces for last 24h and last 7d; p95/p99 calculated by the existing metrics pipeline (verify queries); UX matches mock v2-compact; mobile responsiveness not required.
- Est. effort: 3 dev days + 1 SRE consult.

2) RW-7231: Quick-rollout toolbar (canary toggle + rollback) (H-M)
- Summary: Add a sticky toolbar on rollout detail pages for fast canary toggles and immediate rollback.
- Why: Improves operator time-to-act during incidents; several customers asked for one-click fallbacks.
- Scope: UI control + API call to existing rollout endpoint; soft-confirm modal; telemetry event.
- Wireframe notes: toolbar sits at top right, compact (icon + label), confirmation dialog includes estimated downstream impact.
- Acceptance criteria: rollback API invoked and response handled; audit log entry emitted; unit tests for toolbar state.
- Est. effort: 5 dev days + UX polish.

3) RW-7260: First-class KV cache visibility (M-L)
- Summary: Expose cache hit/miss ratio at model route level with simple toggle to reset local prefix cache.
- Why: Ops frequently ask whether cache is the cause of latency regressions.
- Scope: read-only metrics + flush button that calls existing admin endpoint.
- Acceptance criteria: show 1h/24h cache hit rate; flush button triggers backend and shows toast on success/fail; audit log.
- Est. effort: 2 dev days + 0.5 UX.

4) RW-7312: Rollout-history compact timeline (M-M)
- Summary: Convert the verbose rollout timeline into a compact, scannable UI (compact cards + event summary line).
- Why: PMs want faster triage of what happened during rollouts (who initiated, percent rollout, notes).
- Scope: front-end reflow + reuse existing backend events. No new DB schema.
- Acceptance criteria: timeline renders 30 most recent events; expansion reveals full event payload; performance comparable to current page load.
- Est. effort: 4 dev days.

5) RW-7350: Default model pinning UX (H-H spike)
- Summary: Investigate UX + data model for per-tenant default model pinning and rollout policies.
- Why: Customers want to pin to quantized variants without changing code. This touches backend model mapping.
- Scope: spike only (design + API contract + migration impact doc).
- Acceptance criteria: mockups for console UI, API spec stub, migration risk assessment.
- Est. effort: 5 dev days (spike) + 2 design days.

6) RW-7378: Route-swap preview (low-effort polish)
- Summary: Small change that previews traffic distribution after a planned route swap.
- Why: Prevents human error during manual swaps.
- Scope: overlay showing percentages; no simulation.
- Acceptance criteria: overlay accurate to planned config; accessible label on overlay.
- Est. effort: 1.5 dev days.

7) RW-7409: Console onboard checklist (M-L)
- Summary: Add a first-time checklist for new orgs in console (setup keys, link billing, create first route).
- Why: Reduce onboarding calls; align with PLG goals.
- Scope: simple checklist UI + linkouts to docs; gated until org creates first route.
- Acceptance criteria: checklist appears for new orgs; progress saved; telemetry events for each completed step.
- Est. effort: 2 dev days + copy review.

Wireframe / UX writeups (high level):
- Route-level latency table (RW-7203): mock v2-compact attached in linked PR. Design note: use same color tokens as existing latency charts, but compress vertical spacing. Show sparkline + p95/p99 numbers. Interaction: clicking a route row opens traces panel (deferred).
- Quick-rollout toolbar (RW-7231): mock v1 attached. Design note: need engineering confirmation that the rollback endpoint can return pre-rollback snapshots. If not, add quick snapshot creation step.

Sprint cutlist (proposed May sprint):
- Committed (core): RW-7203, RW-7260, RW-7378, RW-7409
- Stretch (if capacity): RW-7231, RW-7312
- Spike (parallel): RW-7350 (spike only)

Dependencies and risks:
- Metrics queries: RW-7203 & RW-7260 rely on SRE to expose p95/p99 and cache stats at route granularity. Action: SRE to confirm query availability by 2025-05-12 (assigned to Samir).
- Audit log plumbing: RW-7231 + RW-7260 require audit events. Confirm existing endpoint coverage.
- Rollout API contract: RW-7231 needs rollback API idempotency guarantees. Engineering to confirm.

Open questions / notes to follow up:
- Data retention windows for p99 calculation (should we surface 48h or 7d by default?).
- Does the flush-cache action need RBAC beyond current rollout permissions? (Security to advise).
- Mobile UX: defer for now but note usage in internal analytics shows 12% console access from mobile; may need a follow-up ticket.

Next steps:
- Assign owners to tickets in JIRA and add time estimates (PM).
- Samir to confirm metrics availability by 2025-05-12.
- Design to upload final compact mocks for RW-7203 and RW-7231 by 2025-05-09.
- Grooming follow-up meeting: 2025-05-14 10:00 PT (30m) to finalize cutlist and sprint assignments.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep RW-7350 as exploratory — we don't want to bake infra migration decisions into May sprint.
- Prioritize items that unblock CS escalations first.
- When in doubt, scope down: prefer an MLP (minimum lovable product) that can ship in <1 week rather than an incomplete large feature.

End of doc.
